facts.statement: The study found that CXCL9 encourages nerve fiber growth and cell survival in PC12 cells and sympathetic neurons without needing the CXCR3 receptor.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Researchers tested a group of eight different CXCL9 protein versions and peptides to separate the N-terminal core from the C-terminal tail.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: Protein versions missing the C-terminal tail showed no ability to support nerve growth or activate the ERK1/2 and Akt signaling pathways.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The C-terminal tail alone, whether attached to a protein carrier or made as a short peptide, was enough to restore nerve growth, cell survival, and neuron rescue.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The protein carrier used to test the tail had no effect on any of the measured outcomes.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The study concludes that the neurotrophic effects of CXCL9 come specifically from its basic C-terminal tail and not from its standard N-terminal domain.
